_note: Sources for ops/audit-pack-daily.sh. Adding one is a DATA change: no code edit, no redeploy. A disabled source is still printed every run, so it cannot go quietly missing.

sources.note: What the OS already learns about the world each day — framework EOL, API-version drift, deprecated deps, new CVEs. Each finding CLASS is a candidate lens: the audit pack should catch in a client's repo what the watchdog catches in ours.

Ahmad's primary audit source (2026-09-23). Discovery needs a logged-in session, so the cycle lists the profile in a real browser with INSTAGRAM-ONLY cookies, downloads what is new, and sends the AUDIO plus the caption to Gemini. Never the video: one 2.5-minute reel measured 28,626,271 tokens and exhausted the free tier's 250k/day in a single call; the audio track is 687 KB against 37 MB.
What other audit tools started checking. Sunday only — a weekly signal read daily is noise.

Ahmad, 2026-09-23. php-deps pins only four STRUCTURAL facts (no lockfile, PHP floor, framework major, minimum-stability) because it refuses to guess a CVE. This is where verified advisories come from. Recorded to audit-pack-advisories.tsv as DATA and deduped by id; only ONE lens candidate is ever proposed from the whole feed, because filing a lens per CVE would open fifty issues for one idea. The REST API, not advisories.atom: that answers 406 with and without a User-Agent (measured 2026-09-23).

Ahmad, 2026-09-23 — the highest-yield source measured: ONE hand audit of a client Laravel repo (acme-client-audit) produced 11 lenses. Reads '### SEC-004: <title>'-shaped findings out of each client's reports/*.md, reduces the title to a defect CLASS so another client's wording of the same defect does not propose it twice, and skips any class an existing lens already covers.
